title: PY101: Lists and tuples in Python
question: What are a list and a tuple in Python, and how do they differ?
reference_answer: A list is an ordered collection written with square brackets. A tuple is an ordered collection written with parentheses. Lists are mutable, so items can be added, removed or changed. Tuples are immutable, so they cannot change after creation.

submissions.answer: A list is an ordered collection written with square brackets and it is mutable, so you can add, remove or change items. A tuple is an ordered collection written with parentheses and it is immutable, so it cannot change after it is created.
A list uses [] and a tuple uses (). Tuples cannot be changed.
